The check was wrong, not the reading; the declaration's revision records it, logs/reading-1-stopped.log is its log, and its folder (16 GB of raw streams and partly written arrays) was removed whole.

The engine's output norm exists at the answer rows only (and at that one prompt position, which is not kept): there is no native output-normalized state at the question rows. A comparison in output-norm space at question rows has to compose the normalization from the raw last merge or from l_out-34, both kept at every row; the reading cannot hold that composition to the engine there.

Qualified on the original only, on card 0, with this recorder, engine build and driver. That the same reader reads a changed model identically rests on the reader running the same command on another file; no changed model was read here, by the declaration's rule.

The raw source (input-overlap) holds only the attention merges' outputs raw; the feed-forward's and the layer's last merges are held to the baseline through its float32 derivation, bit for bit, and to the engine's own ADD, not to a second raw recording.

The reading takes 12.95 GB for one state (105 arrays of 19,751 by 1,536 float32, and the two terminal ones). With 53 GB free when it ended, 13 above the 40 GiB margin, this disk holds one more state at a time: a sweep that reads many states keeps each only as long as its scorer needs it, or sends it to the bucket first.
what_this_changes: The whole-history scorer's native dependency (SCORING.md, 'Remaining native reader dependency') has its reader and its original reference in one form: the engine's direct state at every merge, at every answer and prompt row, bound to model, recorder, libraries, card, driver and each answer's ending. The original's reading is the same engine output the target factory's source (the baseline) holds, bit for bit, so a target compiled from the baseline and a model read by states_reading.py are compared on one observable, with the float32-against-float64 difference of the feature arithmetic stated (at most 2.6e-07 and 4.5e-07) instead of assumed. It decides nothing about a target, a rule or a construction: binding it into the scorer, and the terminal normalization's composition, are the objective owner's.
